title: Sort Colors
description:
The array nums contains only 0, 1, and 2. Reorder it in place with all zeros first, then ones, then twos, and return the modified array. This exercise grades the returned array, so do not return nothing.

Because there are only three possible values, you can keep boundaries for the finished zero and two regions while scanning the undecided middle. This tests whether you can partition an array without a general-purpose sort or another array.

Example 1:

Input: nums = [2,0,2,1,1,0]
Output: [0,0,1,1,2,2]

Example 2:

Input: nums = [2,0,1]
Output: [0,1,2]

Example 3:

Input: nums = [1,1]
Output: [1,1]

Constraints:

  • 1 <= nums.length <= 300
  • Each nums[i] is 0, 1, or 2.
  • Use O(1) auxiliary space; do not use a built-in sorting function.

exampleTestCases.explanation: The two zeros move ahead of the ones and twos.
All three colors end up in order.
An array of identical colors is unchanged.
